titre: Marvel Boss Officially Reveals Why Avengers Switched from Kang to Doctor Doom
chapo: Marvel Studios boss Kevin Feige says that the studio planned a pivot to Doctor Doom and away from Kang before Jonathan Majors was fired.
extrait: Avengers: Doomsday is a month away and will find the Avengers, the New Avengers, and X-Men from the Fox films facing off against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. Originally, the fifth Avengers film was titled The Kang Dynasty and would have starred Jonathan Majors as Kang, who appeared in Loki and Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania. Marvel fired him in December 2023 after he was convicted on assault and harassment charges, and retooled The Kang Dynasty into the Doctor Doom-centric Doomsday. However, according to Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige, the Marvel Cinematic Universe always would have pivoted to Doom replacing Kang as the next Avengers-level threat, regardless of Majors' legal issues and firing. Speaking with Empire Magazine, Feige revealed the plan to pivot away from Kang began around the release of the third Ant-Man film in early 2023. "Quantumania was not received the way we would have liked," Feige said (via IGN). "There are many elements of that that we're proud of, the Kang performance being one of them. But we were changing [The Kang Dynasty] even at that point. It would still have been called The Kang Dynasty, but it would have been a set-up for Doom, midway through that movie." Majors' Kang the Conqueror variant was the villain of Quantumania after Kang first appeared as He Who Remains in Loki season 1. Much like how Josh Brolin's Thanos appeared throughout the MCU before going toe-to-toe with the Avengers in Avengers: Infinity War and Endgame, Kang was being established as an overarching antagonist before The Kang Dynasty. In contrast to them, Doom has been haphazardly established in the MCU via post-credits scenes in 2025's The Fantastic Four: First Steps and the recent re-release of Endgame. Setting up Doom in a film titled The Kang Dynasty would have been a bold move. From the public's point of view, it certainly seemed like Marvel retooled the Avengers films in response to Majors' convictions. However, according to Feige, that wasn't exactly the case. "We didn't want to rush into any rash decisions in terms of employment. People think there was a cause-and-effect with Jonathan's issues, and that certainly accelerated some things. But the Doom of it all was well underway before that." Marvel is known for deception and trickery, so you're well within your rights to doubt Feige's comments here. titre: Marvel Boss Kevin Feige Addresses Jonathan Majors' Firing, Insists It Was Always the Plan to Eventually Replace Kang With Doctor Doom
chapo: Kang was always set to be replaced by Doctor Doom as the main villain of the Multiverse Saga, Marvel boss Kevin Feige has insisted — regardless of Jonathan Majors' high-profile firing.
extrait: Kang was already set to be replaced by Doctor Doom as the main villain of the Multiverse Saga, Marvel boss Kevin Feige has insisted — regardless of Jonathan Majors' high-profile firing. Before Majors' swift ditching by Disney in the wake of assault and harassment charges, the Multiverse Saga's first Avengers movie was due to be titled The Kang Dynasty, with Majors' Kang the Conqueror taking on Earth's mightiest heroes in a Thanos-style role. The film was instead subsequently retooled and retitled as Avengers: Doomsday, with Robert Downey Jr. then announced as returning. But rather than this pivot being completely unplanned, Feige has now claimed the change had already been on the cards — even if the way it was presented was disrupted after Majors' exit. Indeed, Feige argued that Doom's introduction was already being hurried along after the failure of Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania, which underperformed at the box office despite featuring Kang front and center. "Quantumania was not received the way we would have liked," Feige told Empire magazine. "There are many elements of that that we're proud of, the Kang performance being one of them. But we were changing [The Kang Dynasty] even at that point. It would still have been called The Kang Dynasty, but it would have been a set-up for Doom, midway through that movie." The interview marks the first time Feige has properly addressed Majors' departure in detail. Disney parted ways with the rising star immediately after he was found guilty of assaulting his then-girlfriend, though there had been a growing expectation in the lead-up to Majors' sentencing that the problematic actor was set to be jettisoned. Still, questions remained over how Marvel would handle the Kang storyline, which had been heavily seeded in Loki and elsewhere by that point. "It was very delicate," Feige continued. "We didn't want to rush into any rash decisions in terms of employment. People think there was a cause-and-effect with Jonathan's issues, and that certainly accelerated some things. But the Doom of it all was well underway before that." Will Doomsday address Kang at all? This remains to be seen, though Marvel's policy up until now appears to be ignoring that the Kang storyline ever took place, in favor of Doctor Doom instead. Avengers: Doomsday is set to premiere December 18, 2026, meaning we're only weeks away from its release date. chapo: It was in the works long before Jonathan Majors' firing

Kevin Feige has revealed that the pivot to Avengers: Doomsday from The Kang Dynasty was not as surprising as it first seemed. The Marvel head explained that they were always considering bringing Doctor Doom in "midway" during the movie. Speaking to Empire magazine, he said (H/T The Playlist): "It probably would still have been called The Kang Dynasty, but it would have been a set-up for Doom, midway through that movie," adding that they first approached Robert Downey Jr's agent at the Ant-Man And The Wasp: Quantumania premiere. Feige went on to confirm that the situation around Jonathan Majors' exit from Marvel was "delicate". The actor was dropped by Marvel after he was found guilty of assault in December 2023. "We didn't want to rush into any rash decisions in terms of employment. People think there was a cause-and-effect with Jonathan's issues, and that certainly accelerated some things. But the Doom of it all was well underway before that." Avengers: Doomsday sees Downey Jr. return to the MCU in a new role, becoming the biggest villain that the heroes have faced yet. In order to defeat him, three different universes (the OG MCU, the Fantastic Four, and the Fox X-Men universe) are all teaming up. However, in the meantime, it seems like Doom has been assembling his own team composed of the Hulk and Scarlet Witch… One thing we do know is that Doom is not a Tony Stark variant in the new movie. Not sure yet what that means about their shared resemblance, but in Feige we trust… Avengers: Doomsday arrives in UK cinemas on December 16 and US theaters on December 18.
